approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule by sampling local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It sanitizes and normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch allowed by its short-term inverse-motif memory. A fresh neighbor is blocked when opposite signed motif changes match restrictions from one earlier selected transition. The walk then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening move, uses canonical order for exact ties and maintains a separate best archive. Selected transitions install bounded, sign-balanced restrictions with four-step tenure and latest-origin overlap refresh. Identity repair and the nitrogen-relocation menu are retained parts of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Remove active tabu rejection for one integration contribution probe. The same motif predicate and memory history will still be recorded, allowing every evaluated neighbor that the retained rule would have blocked to be identified. The evaluated batch will instead be the first full set of valid fresh graph neighbors. Earlier siblings relaxed matching, changed which transitions or motifs received credit, preserved overlapping origins or extended restriction lifetime; each kept an active tabu gate. This experiment tests the contribution of that entire admission gate after nitrogen-relocation development. The earlier relaxation losses motivate a predicted score decrease when the gate is removed.

hypothesis: Ablate enforcement of the retained same-transition bidirectional inverse-motif tabu gate: every graph-valid canonically fresh neighbor reaches the inherited first-full-batch admission path, while the unchanged Parent predicate and selected-transition memory lifecycle run only as passive diagnostics.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu removal admits 170 otherwise vetoed neighbors and lowers the mean score by 0.002275
finding_summary.insights: The active gate provides a small net endpoint benefit in this panel despite excluding some immediate improvements and even one molecule that becomes a Child task maximum. The result therefore rules out judging the gate solely by the quality of its excluded neighbors or by counts of local gains. Its effect develops through changed batch membership, random-stream consumption and later sources: every paired session first diverged at a common recorded neighbor vetoed by Parent and admitted by Child, but the next state sometimes stayed identical for several more batches. The effect is strongly seed- and task-dependent; the average loss is dominated by the second seed, especially sitagliptin_mpo, while two seeds improve. This is evidence for the entire gate in the tested panel, not universal necessity or an individual motif contribution. Removing restrictions also did not guarantee greater access to the retained nitrogen exchange: eligible source batches fell from 97 to 49 and accepted exchanges from ten to four; none of the four beat its source or was selected. Chemistry remained mixed. Similar typical size and ring counts conceal more peroxide and sulfur-triple-bond products alongside fewer nitrogen- and oxygen-halogen bonds; 80 of the 170 bypass admissions carry at least one defined concern marker. High labels do not establish stability or feasible geometry. Finally, all 135 affected Child batches stop with only six to nine observed retained-gate alternatives, so their unobserved replacements and alternative winners remain unknown.
finding_summary.results: Removal was exercised throughout the panel. All 435 batches contained the first ten valid fresh neighbors, with zero active tabu rejections, compared with 195 rejections in the Parent. The unchanged predicate identified 170 evaluated neighbors it would have vetoed on the actual Child history, spread over 135 batches and all 15 task sessions. Of these, 23 beat their source, 12 tied and 135 lost; nine strictly improved the archive and 29 became the next state. Across all proposals, source wins rose from 468 to 496 and strict archive updates from 238 to 269. Nevertheless, final macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519484, a decrease of 0.002275 that narrowly meets the registered 0.002 prediction. Seed deltas were +0.021475, -0.037773 and +0.009471; their population deviation was 0.025574. Task mean changes were +0.006636 for zaleplon_mpo, -0.008325 for deco_hop, +0.039404 for drd2_docking, +0.007223 for median_2 and -0.056314 for sitagliptin_mpo. All runs completed with full validity. Raw generation attempts fell from 5303 to 5123, while recorded task runtime rose from 82.59 to 100.20 seconds.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring families persist alongside peroxide bridges, reactive heteroatom halides and densely connected sulfur cages.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-045725e4628f was assessed against Parent n-abcd951ab7cc using the complete supplied seed panel: all fifteen trajectories per node, with 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. The digest lists no tasks without trajectories. The bounded best and final excerpts are not balanced across seeds, so the seed descriptions below also use the full trajectories. Every cited SMILES is from the authoritative digest. The generated chemistry is ring-rich, with substantial aromatic content, carbonyls, amines, ethers, halogens and sulfur. Every task has ring-closure and branch token rates of 1.0; aromatic-token rates range from 0.8414 to 1.0. These are molecule-level string-presence rates, not fractions of atoms or chemically proven aromatic rings. Passive RDKit reading of the Child proposals gives 21–52 heavy atoms and 1–10 perceived basis rings, with medians of 33 and 4. The Parent has corresponding ranges of 21–53 and 2–10, with the same medians. Distinct seed walks reach different frameworks, but the best excerpts often contain closely related variants of one framework. Chemical plausibility is mixed and often poor near the observed maxima. Under identical graph-marker definitions, Child versus Parent proposals containing an O–O single bond number 360 versus 55; sulfur triple bonds 187 versus 95; N–halogen bonds 383 versus 500; O–halogen bonds 189 versus 301; and hydrogen-bearing sulfur with total valence above two 1234 versus 1247. These overlapping markers describe structures, not measured reactivity. The O–O motif persists in 33 Child selected states versus no Parent selected states. Among the 170 accepted Child molecules tagged by the saved logs as retained-predicate would-veto admissions, 80 carry at least one of the defined concern markers; their median size and ring count are 32.5 heavy atoms and 4 basis rings. This subset is not chemically clean and does not establish an individual motif contribution. All task digests have charge and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 3318 of the 4350 Child proposals, while no proposal has a stored atom chiral tag. Formal neutrality does not mean that an amine could not protonate. Four accepted Child molecules are logged direct aromatic nitrogen positional exchanges, compared with ten in the Parent; this narrow subset does not characterize whole-walk chemistry. The passive audit and definitions are recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0013-02-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. No candidate execution, new molecule generation, scoring, conformer calculation or synthetic route assessment was performed. The observations support missing chemical controls and comparisons, not a known absent target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals contain 21–30 heavy atoms and 1–5 RDKit basis rings; the typical framework has three rings. Indole or benzothiophene cores carry an aryl carboxamide, with methoxy/ethoxy, methyl, amino, hydroxy or thiol substitutions. liabilities: The maximum contains an N–Cl hydrazide and a benzylic halide; the latter is a potential electrophilic site, while the N–Cl connection is a chemical-stability concern.

The digest also includes a ring-embedded C–S triple bond at hydrogen-bearing sulfur, hydroxylamine/hydrazine connections, disrupted aromatic rings and a strained small-ring aniline variant. Passing a molecular parser does not establish their synthetic feasibility.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu removal admits 170 otherwise vetoed neighbors and lowers the mean score by 0.002275
finding_summary.insights: The active gate provides a small net endpoint benefit in this panel despite excluding some immediate improvements and even one molecule that becomes a Child task maximum. The result therefore rules out judging the gate solely by the quality of its excluded neighbors or by counts of local gains. Its effect develops through changed batch membership, random-stream consumption and later sources: every paired session first diverged at a common recorded neighbor vetoed by Parent and admitted by Child, but the next state sometimes stayed identical for several more batches. The effect is strongly seed- and task-dependent; the average loss is dominated by the second seed, especially sitagliptin_mpo, while two seeds improve. This is evidence for the entire gate in the tested panel, not universal necessity or an individual motif contribution. Removing restrictions also did not guarantee greater access to the retained nitrogen exchange: eligible source batches fell from 97 to 49 and accepted exchanges from ten to four; none of the four beat its source or was selected. Chemistry remained mixed. Similar typical size and ring counts conceal more peroxide and sulfur-triple-bond products alongside fewer nitrogen- and oxygen-halogen bonds; 80 of the 170 bypass admissions carry at least one defined concern marker. finding_summary.headline: Tabu removal admits 170 otherwise vetoed neighbors and lowers the mean score by 0.002275
finding_summary.insights: The active gate provides a small net endpoint benefit in this panel despite excluding some immediate improvements and even one molecule that becomes a Child task maximum. The result therefore rules out judging the gate solely by the quality of its excluded neighbors or by counts of local gains. Its effect develops through changed batch membership, random-stream consumption and later sources: every paired session first diverged at a common recorded neighbor vetoed by Parent and admitted by Child, but the next state sometimes stayed identical for several more batches. The effect is strongly seed- and task-dependent; the average loss is dominated by the second seed, especially sitagliptin_mpo, while two seeds improve. This is evidence for the entire gate in the tested panel, not universal necessity or an individual motif contribution. Removing restrictions also did not guarantee greater access to the retained nitrogen exchange: eligible source batches fell from 97 to 49 and accepted exchanges from ten to four; none of the four beat its source or was selected. Chemistry remained mixed. Similar typical size and ring counts conceal more peroxide and sulfur-triple-bond products alongside fewer nitrogen- and oxygen-halogen bonds; 80 of the 170 bypass admissions carry at least one defined concern marker. High labels do not establish stability or feasible geometry. Finally, all 135 affected Child batches stop with only six to nine observed retained-gate alternatives, so their unobserved replacements and alternative winners remain unknown.
finding_summary.results: Removal was exercised throughout the panel. All 435 batches contained the first ten valid fresh neighbors, with zero active tabu rejections, compared with 195 rejections in the Parent. The unchanged predicate identified 170 evaluated neighbors it would have vetoed on the actual Child history, spread over 135 batches and all 15 task sessions. Of these, 23 beat their source, 12 tied and 135 lost; nine strictly improved the archive and 29 became the next state. Across all proposals, source wins rose from 468 to 496 and strict archive updates from 238 to 269. Nevertheless, final macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519484, a decrease of 0.002275 that narrowly meets the registered 0.002 prediction. Seed deltas were +0.021475, -0.037773 and +0.009471; their population deviation was 0.025574. Task mean changes were +0.006636 for zaleplon_mpo, -0.008325 for deco_hop, +0.039404 for drd2_docking, +0.007223 for median_2 and -0.056314 for sitagliptin_mpo. All runs completed with full validity. Raw generation attempts fell from 5303 to 5123, while recorded task runtime rose from 82.59 to 100.20 seconds.
